cards.title: Artifact Constitution separates source, durable evidence, generated output, and local runtime state
cards.summary: The Artifact Constitution defines source artifacts, durable evidence, generated artifacts, and local runtime artifacts, and requires validation after file-creating tools. It keeps framework, registry, and tools versioned while excluding generated observability ledgers, legacy command adapters, and machine-local runtime state by default.
cards.selection_reason: Runtime and inventory refresh work must know which files are source, durable evidence, generated output, or local state before validating changes.

claim_shape.object_ref: source, durable evidence, generated output, and local runtime state
claim_shape.non_authority_notice: This card summarizes governance behavior; the Artifact Constitution remains canonical.

residue.note: Generated observability indexes and local runtime folders should not become inventory source by accident.

cards.title: Durable runtime handoff keeps orchestrator meaning separate from adapter execution
cards.summary: The durable runtime lets orchestrators hand off work through `RUNTIME-HANDOFF.md`, `tools/arcanum --exec`, and adapter-selected execution. Orchestrators own workflow meaning, `tools/arcanum` owns command resolution and adapter selection, and adapters own runtime-specific translation and outcome classification.

source_refs.selector: model, ownership, run folder, status model
schema discipline, adapters, runtime config, commands

cards.selection_reason: Implementation agents need the runtime ownership boundary before using or documenting command execution surfaces.

claim_shape.object_ref: orchestrator meaning, command resolution, adapter execution, and runtime status
claim_shape.non_authority_notice: This card indexes runtime handoff behavior; framework runtime docs remain canonical.

residue.note: Codex, Claude, and Copilot are host surfaces, not the Arcanum runtime model itself.

cards.title: Observability support stores central signals and rebuildable indexes while keeping observation non-mutating
cards.summary: Framework observability defines meaningful execution signals, central JSONL ledger ownership, rebuildable by-sigil/by-capability indexes, invocation envelope shape, observer role, and reflection triggers. Observers classify gaps and recommend reflection but should not directly rewrite the observed sigil.

source_refs.selector: what to observe and where signals belong

cards.selection_reason: Whole-Arcanum readiness depends on knowing how telemetry and reflection evidence should be represented without treating generated ledgers as source.

claim_shape.object_ref: central signals, rebuildable indexes, observer gaps, and reflection triggers
claim_shape.non_authority_notice: This card summarizes observability support; framework observability docs remain canonical.

residue.note: The central ledger is source of truth; by-sigil and by-capability indexes are rebuildable generated views.

cards.title: Registry files are quick-reference navigation, not canonical capability contracts
cards.summary: The sigil registry is a quick-reference index that summarizes what each sigil does, when to use it, tier, and folder. It also records entry requirements and a maintenance rule, but full instructions remain in the referenced sigil folders.
cards.selection_reason: Agents should use registry files for discovery and navigation while opening canonical skill files for execution authority.

claim_shape.object_ref: discoverable sigil folders and usage summaries
claim_shape.non_authority_notice: Registry entries are navigation summaries; referenced sigil folders remain canonical.

residue.note: Registry updates should follow capability additions, removals, renames, moves, or material purpose changes.

cards.title: Native runtime packages replace legacy command files as the live invocation surface
cards.summary: `tools/arcanum` still documents deterministic capability listing, resolution, and adapter handoff mechanics, but whole-Arcanum Inventory no longer treats `.codex/commands` as source evidence. Live behavior should be tested through canonical source contracts and generated native skill packages, with legacy command files excluded unless a future migration explicitly promotes one as durable evidence.

source_refs.selector: usage, command surface, adapters, and command resolution setup

cards.selection_reason: The agent-fast inventory needs to preserve the boundary between current native skill invocation and legacy command-file adapters before using runtime surfaces as evidence.

claim_shape.object_ref: legacy command-file invocation for Inventory live proof
claim_shape.non_authority_notice: Runtime adapters expose capabilities; canonical behavior remains in source skill and spell contracts plus generated native runtime packages.

residue.note: Legacy command files are not part of the live Inventory promotion proof; use native skill packages and canonical source contracts for cross-repository testing.
